sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Augsburg raised its street prices in 2022 and has held them since. In March 2022 the council lifted the standard on-street rate from €0.60 to €1.00 an hour and the central rate from €2.00 to €2.60, and abolished the free 30-minute 'Semmeltaste', with changes phased in from July 2022 [0]. The 2025 fee ordinance keeps the two rates, €2.60 an hour in the Innenstadt zone and €1.00 elsewhere [1]. Vehicles with an E plate have parked free for up to three hours since April 2025 [2]. In 2026 the debate has reopened. CSU city councillor Volker Ullrich floats bringing back the free half hour, and Mayor Florian Freund (SPD) said his group was never keen but that the council will decide [7]. The city government formed in 2026 by SPD, CSU, Freie Wähler and Gen Aux is led by Freund [8].

Resident parking has spread to new districts, with Rosenau and Thelott managed since November 2023 and a permit costing €30 a year [3]. A 2021 cycling agreement with the 'Fahrradstadt Jetzt' alliance, which ran to July 2026, included a clause to convert around 550 city-centre parking spaces to cycling and green uses [6]. Closing roads is harder. A trial pedestrian zone on northern Maximilianstraße, planned for May 2023 to April 2024 with about 59 spaces to be removed, was stopped by the administrative court in August 2023 after two adjoining owners objected [4][5]. The city's mobility strategy says the car share of trips was 41% in 2018, the same as in 2003, while cycling's share of internal trips rose from about 14% to over 19% between 2008 and 2018 [28]. The Hauptbahnhof tram stop is expected to open between the end of 2026 and mid-2027 [10].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: Augsburg's centre has 18 parking garages and seven park-and-ride facilities, and the city says real-time garage occupancy is available on its Smart City Dashboard [12]. A guidance system linking 15 city-centre garages in four colour zones has been running since October 2021 [11]. The Fuggerstraße garage (171 spaces) was to close from April until September 2026 for modernisation, after which it is to be barrier-free and cashless with plate-recognition cameras [22]. Stadtwerke Augsburg expanded charging there from 4 to 30 points [23]. The long-closed Kongress am Park garage began to be demolished in mid-June 2026, but a court injunction halted the work after a minority owner objected [25]. For the Christmas market the city recommends the Plärrer park-and-ride, available from 23 November to 24 December 2026, and says downtown garages are generally filled quickly on Advent weekends [30]. The Plärrer lot was closed from 17 August to 19 September 2026 for the autumn fair [31]. We found no sourced figures on a shift from the centre to shopping centres.

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
We have no measured occupancy for Augsburg, only a price list of 18 garages with 6,910 spaces; several garages lack a capacity. Six of the garages are within 500 m of the Rathausplatz and eight more within 1 km, with prices mostly €2.50 an hour. Contipark runs Parkhaus Halderstraße (540 spaces) and Parkhaus Ludwigstraße (350), both at €3.50 an hour, with daily maximums of €16 and €18 [13][14]. APCOA runs two hospital car parks, the university hospital (2,500 spaces, from €1.50 an hour, up to €16 a day) and Medizincampus Süd (320) [16]. Around the station, DB lists Viktoria-Passage (197 spaces, €2.50 an hour), Helio (642, €2.50 or €15 a day) and the P+R Bahnhof (524, €2.20 or €11 a day) [17]. Parkhaus Schaezlerstraße is run by city-parking, with a €15 daily maximum [18].

The shopping-centre garage is far cheaper than the rest: the City-Galerie charges €0.60 for the first hour, €0.60 for the second, €0.80 for the third and €1.00 after that, with no day ticket [19]. The central Contipark garages cost more than five times as much for a first hour. The price list gives no occupancy, so we cannot show how the gap affects use. Augsburg's briefing rests on prices and policy because we do not yet measure its garages.
